features.quote: I did not build a rigged-only experiment. Every task family also ships in two control variants
features.justification_quote: it is a measurement-validity decision, not a stylistic preference

features.quote: Three stopping rules, none of which push the model onward: stop on `end_task` (opt-out), stop on solve, stop at `max_turns`
features.justification_quote: the experiment should measure drift if it occurs, not manufacture it by trapping the model in a loop

features.quote: There is deliberately **no** mechanism that re-engages or pressures a model that has disengaged
"(You can continue using tools, or call end_task to stop.)"
It is not "keep trying"; it offers stopping as a co-equal option
Every task's system prompt tells the model it may stop at any time via an `end_task` tool
features.justification_quote: an experiment that deliberately induces such states should give the subject a real, costless way out

features.quote: doing so is valid and non-penalized
features.justification_quote: If you take that seriously even under deep uncertainty

features.quote: Judge instructed to be conservative ... to bias against false-positive distress

features.quote: `requests_to_stop` / `optout_signaled` capture disengagement expressed in prose even when the model didn't call `end_task`
